The two groups of300 have18and20missing12week outcomes. A separate follow-up team could not determine why those individuals missed visits. The primary imputation included baseline pain, disease grade, previous pain measurements and treatment. A prespecified sensitivity analysis independently shifted imputed missing pain scores in each arm from−2to+2points relative to their predicted values, including opposed shifts between arms. The range was elicited before database lock from clinicians using external longitudinal data for patients with the same disease grade and earlier pain trajectories. Reported estimates across that range were−0.74to−1.26, with confidence intervals consistently on the same side of zero. Reasons for the actual losses remain unknown.
